general.description: Substrate-dependent fungal-like organisms that grow deep within planetary crusts. They extend reproductive structures to the surface, typically in elevated terrain such as mountains, cliffs, and crater edges. Energy is derived from chemosynthetic and thermosynthetic processes within the substrate.
environmental_context: Most commonly found in mountainous or high-elevation terrain
Often located in canyons, cliffs, and plateau edges
Subsurface organism with surface reproductive structures only
Frequently coexists with Frutexa in similar biomes

color_variants.rule: Color depends on rare planetary materials (not star type in canonical behavior)

Fungoida bullarum.description: Bubble-like clustered growth structures emerging from a central stalk, adapted for wind-based spore dispersal.

Fungoida gelata.description: Jellyfish-like structure emerging from subterranean mass, releasing floating reproductive tissue.

Fungoida setisis.description: Vertical clustered stalk formations with detachable spore pods designed for dispersal.

Fungoida stabitis.description: Stable column-like growth structure producing dense cylindrical reproductive clusters.

special_rules: Subsurface organism: only reproductive structures are visible on surface
Primary spawn locations are high elevation terrains (mountains, cliffs, plateaus)
Minimum sample distance is 300m due to colony clustering behavior
CO2-based species require strict temperature range (180K–195K)
Fungoida often co-locates with Frutexa in similar biomes
Color is driven by planetary rare materials, not species identity
Terrain accessibility strongly affects perceived spawn density
